notes.note: Titan accepts the missing semi-colon between two assignment statements; Titan treats statement semi-colons as optional (the BNF also writes [SemiColon]), but A.1.2 only allows omission before or after '}'.
Broader reading chosen: semi-colon omitted for the last statement in a block, the last component variable declaration and the last return statement before '}'.

Reading: every list whose BNF allows a variable number of items (enumeration list, component extends list before '{', const list before ';', formal and actual parameter lists before ')'). Titan does not implement trailing commas, hence its syntax errors.
Reading: comments may appear wherever whitespace may appear between lexical elements (not inside tokens or string literals).
Negative test: a block comment that is never closed by '*/' swallows the rest of the module.
Ellipsis tested via a variadic parameter (clause 5.4.3), written as '...' per table A.2 (BNF rule 613 shows the Unicode character U+2026). Titan does not support variadic parameters.
noexecution because decoding needs a codec. Titan uses '=>' for its own class-cast syntax and does not implement the decoded field reference of clause 7.3.
noexecution because invoking ??? causes a runtime error unless the tool provides an implementation (clause 16.1.6). Titan does not implement the not-implemented function.
Reading: only identifier parts of modifiers that are not reserved words (lazy, fuzzy, nocase, index, decoded) are used as ordinary identifiers.
The list of reserved words cannot be tested as a whole; the test checks one sample word (nowait) is rejected as an identifier.
Titan accepts 'timestamp' as an identifier because it does not reserve the extension package keywords of table A.5; the standard forbids it.

Uses the real-time extension keyword 'now' written as 'NOW'; that is not a keyword and is an undefined identifier, so the module must be rejected. This test only makes sense for tools that support the real-time extension.
